translations.text: There is no trickery or falsehood, nor anything of which we say, “It does not exist,” while it exists all the more.
For who will be able to bear speaking of them? Or who will endure hearing them, especially if we reveal them all?
Should the discourse now cleanse us of our sins, or hand us over because of them through parables, riddles, and examples?

I do not understand. For it is he who takes the initiative with those who will behave like animals at the proper time, whether it is the mother or the children. He says through the prophet, “Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce by which I sent her away? Or to whom did I sell you?”
Look, I have handed you over because of your sins, and because of your lawless acts I have cast out your mother.

Woe to us! For the heaven of heavens and everything in them, the earth and the depths, the mountains, the sea, and all creation and everything in them praise the Lord God and give him glory, but human beings insult him by their acts of ungodliness.

Do we not hear the day of creation blessing God and giving praise? Or they bless him and exalt him above all forever. Yet the voice of many among humanity fills the whole world as they bless him with their tongues and with words alone, while we insult him through unnatural acts.
Also, [?] subject to creation, so that the Lord says, “It is good,” as it is written: “God saw everything he had made, and behold, it was very good.”
Oh, the rebelliousness and disobedience of human beings, which leads God to say that they are evil in his sight!
All creation is good, as he said from the beginning. But as for human beings, for whose sake he brought creation into being, only a few out of many are those upon whom the will
of their maker rests, so that they are good as they ought to be. One must not say that humanity is evil, because the Creator formed it very good.
Will they say, or have they said, that any one of the created things is God’s offspring, or a member of his body?
And how are human beings not even more excellent, since they are God’s offspring, members of Christ, and the dwelling place of his Spirit?
Is a house built for its own sake alone? Or is a lamp lit for the sake of its own light?
Again, which is superior: the house, or the person for whom it was built? The light of the lamp, or the person?
And how are human beings not great and very highly honored, since the Lord God created heaven and built the world for their sake, and brought lights into existence for their sake?
Yet we mistreat human beings, God’s offspring, through unnatural acts, without fear.
For sin has made the human being fail to recognize that he comes from God and is a child of God.

Was the outer scaffolding set up so that someone would not climb up on it? For it is a house of clay, bricks, stones, and the other building materials. But the scaffolding that is inside [?] there, so that they will [?] themselves upward [?] the height upon them.
For just as no one can climb up the outside upright or confidently without scaffolding, or perhaps on a ladder, taking care not to fall,

so it is even more impossible for what is being built on the inside—that is, the human being—to find a place of rest on the day of distress without understanding what is written for them, or reading [?]
For how, even if they make many turns until they climb up on the outside, [?] what is being constructed inside—that is, the human being, whether male or female—there is no [?]
for work. Nor is there any other rule or any other way of being reconciled to God besides keeping his laws. And without the Scriptures no one can raise their heart
out of unnatural ways and make it rise above them in purity. Nor will their heart ever be free of earthly things so that they may be with Christ in heaven.
And how, when they leave the body, will they go to the Lord? Or where will they find him, if they did not make him their helper on earth [?]

So that he will help him on the [?] day of great distress. For those whom he now saves from abomination are also those whom he will help all the more at the time when there is no deed to do and no word to say, except for his mercy alone.
For it is a matter or a decree: no father or mother, no brother or sister, no son or daughter, no friend, no money or wealth, nothing
Among all those you can think of, or those you cannot think of, [?] will be able to rescue us from him. Rather, it is necessary that those in the inhabited world [?]
Look: “Open to us!” And then, did they open? Or did they not hear this: “I do not know you”?
Why? Is it not because the time to go and buy oil is different from the time for those who have prepared themselves to go in?
Those who go in through the door are quite different from those who turn back from the door to go and prepare themselves.
The former did not knock; they went in joyfully.
Or why would they knock when the door was open?

The latter knocked, but the door was not opened to them. They were foolish, because standing at the door saying many words is one thing, when they do not have the gift for the master of the house in their hands; going in with the gift is another, with the gift having preceded them.
For the things the outer house lacks—that is, things that have not been painted on it or completed in it—in the same way, among the things I am thinking of, neither [?]
Consider, then, the minds of the builders, the carpenters, those who fashion iron, and those who paint or decorate,
I will add them still more abundantly to the inner one.

for they belong to him and are attached to him, and they exist because of him, with every skill and every boast, in every work through which he will make them famous, or they will spread his fame throughout the whole earth
and speak about him everywhere through [?]. Those far away and those nearby will hear about him, especially those who see him. These are walls surrounding him, places
for shooting arrows, towers, spears, swords, arrows, bows, axes, weapons, helmets, belts, armor, sandals of iron and bronze,
slings, stones, torches, lamps—because it is not only during the day that the enemies of Christ’s soldier prowl about, but even more at night—

shields, lances like the one with which Phinehas quenched God’s anger, coats of mail, brick battlements, every kind of military equipment against the rulers, the authorities, and the world-rulers of darkness,

against the spiritual forces of evil; true measures like the one by which the saints stood; the pattern of judgments without favoritism; the sign of God’s coming judgment; the image of wakefulness, vigilance, and wisdom.

and above all, the testimony concerning those who work in them: if they forget them, to their own ruin and defilement, the things they build for themselves will bring shame and disgrace upon them in the days when he examines them.
If it is permissible to set up seats in the outer part for those who will sit on them or read aloud from them, it is all the more permissible to set up thrones in the inner part
for the one who will sit on them and hear and see what the servant does and what he will say, and give judgment in favor of the one being treated unjustly.
People are stationed to guard the outside and protect it because of those who come into it every day, and to protect it because of those who live in it.

Did they paint the likeness of the pattern of every kind of equipment they worked with, or of what surrounded him, while each person devoted himself to his work, with his sword at his neck and in his hands and over every working tool? Was he not building?
Nor will anything be established in it, especially for someone to live in it, teach, give judgment, or do even a single good thing.

And there is a fear that they may not have supplied other things with which to work on the interior, because they have not gathered them all together, and so they may lack what is needed for their construction.
And not only are they not all complete, but one has tilted, another is not properly spread out, and another has had its walls split apart.
And they broke apart from one another because they were not bound together. Another fell by himself. Some fell on one another and became a single heap of ruins.
And others, again, who fell out of it fell onto some of those outside it,
and the things built outside it fell down onto the things being built within it, all of them suffering this same destruction because of negligence.
For there are wood of every kind and iron to make them firm, just like those secured in it. Neither the wind, nor the waves, nor the rain, nor the river could shake them.

For they are bound together on every side, from their summits to their foundations, and their tops all around, while their courses bind them to one another—the wooden ones and the stone ones, together with all their equipment—and without denying the truth or opposing what is right.
truly.
